title: Workspace-sync cost audit — week-1 PROP-101 data shows workspace-sync at ~$13/day ($2.18/run × 41 runs/week, 21 turns/run, 24% output fraction) — surprisingly expensive for a 'sync' agent. Audit what each cycle is actually doing in the LLM, and propose what (if anything) can be slimmed without losing the rescue / propagation guarantees.
context:
Week-1 cost-history.jsonl analysis (2026-06-14 → 2026-06-20):

  Agent             $/run    runs   $/week  composition
  workspace-sync   $2.18      41    $89    49% cache_write, 27% cache_read, 24% output
  curmudgeon       $11.62     12    $139   50% cache_write, 37% read, 14% out
  analyst          $9.61       6    $58    48% cache_write, 38% read, 14% out
  decider          $7.01       9    $63    30% write, 52% read, 18% out
  ...

Workspace-sync ranks #2 by WEEKLY total, eclipsing analyst-baby ($3/day), social ($2/day), and poller ($2/day). For an agent that's nominally a Haiku/Sonnet file-mover this is the surprise of the cost data.

Distinguishing features:
  - 21 turns per run. For comparison, dome-mirror (sibling sync agent) runs 5 turns at $0.73/run. 21 vs 5 is a 4× turn-count difference.
  - 24% output fraction — that's quite high. Suggests workspace-sync is WRITING a lot per cycle. The 65,000 resurrection-skips per cycle we documented yesterday is consistent — each skip is a tool_result + a follow-up assistant decision turn.
  - 49% cache_write — half its cost is invalidating-and-rebuilding cache. Same pattern PROP-021 attacks on curmudgeon (where shipping Phase 2 stage 2 is the leveraged fix). For workspace-sync, the cause is likely 'the workspace state differs every cycle so cache invalidates every run' — structural, harder to slim.
  - 49 cache_write + 27 cache_read = 76% of cost is cache machinery. Only 24% is genuine new work (output). For a 'sync' agent that should ideally be deterministic, this ratio is upside-down.

The surprise factor matters: nobody designed workspace-sync to be a high-cost agent. The cost crept up as the resurrection-skips set grew (65K skip events/cycle now vs presumably 1-2K when workspace-sync was first deployed). PROP-094/099/103 added the skip-and-log discipline; the unintended side-effect is making the LLM walk a much longer list.

Other-side check the operator already considered:
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'workspace-sync is doing real work — file-by-file rescue logic with guards is genuinely complex.' Counter: a lot of the per-cycle work is checking the same 60K+ files against the same prune-deleted set. That's mechanical and could probably move to a script the LLM only consults for exceptions.
- ARGUE-AGAINST: '$13/day is small relative to curmudgeon and analyst.' Counter: $13/day = $4.7K/year of operator spend on what should be a deterministic sync. Even halving it = $2.3K/year saved.
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Touching workspace-sync is the PROP-051 disaster vector.' Counter: investigation is read-only. Any proposed slim ships in shadow + extensive smoke-test per PROP-051 lessons. Acknowledge the risk; don't let it block the investigation.
task: Investigate workspace-sync's per-cycle cost composition with the same discipline as PROP-021's curmudgeon dispatcher analysis. Map what each of the 21 turns/run is doing. Identify which steps consume the most input tokens (the cache_write driver) and which produce the most output (the 24% output fraction). Propose Phase 0 measurement + Phase 1 precompute-or-slim if a clear lever exists. Honor PROP-051 disaster-sensitive constraint: propose-only; operator integrates after smoke-test.
investigation_questions: Q1 — Per-turn token attribution. Add cheap STEP_MARKER instrumentation (mirror PROP-104 Phase 0's pattern in decider.md) to workspace-sync.md major steps: clone setup → smart_copy loop → step 4c sync-workspace → step 5 commit → step 6 push. Capture 3-5 runs of per-step input/cache/output volume. Surface the top-2 steps by token cost.

Q2 — Resurrection-skip volume attribution. The 65K-skip-per-cycle workload looks like the prime suspect for the output volume. Confirm or refute: instrument the smart_copy loop to count skip-decisions per category (older-than-prune-retention vs PROP-094 git-deleted-authoritative vs git-append-only-matches vs etc). If skips dominate the LLM turn count, the lever is 'move the bulk decision out of the LLM and only consult the LLM on exceptions.' If skips are NOT the dominant cost, look elsewhere.

Q3 — Compare to dome-mirror. dome-mirror does git→FUSE propagation (companion to workspace-sync's FUSE→git direction) at 5 turns/run on Sonnet. Why is workspace-sync 4× the turn count? Is dome-mirror missing some discipline workspace-sync has, or is workspace-sync doing 4× the work, or are the cadences structurally different?

Q4 — Helper-script extraction candidates. PROP-066 / PROP-021 / PROP-104 set the precedent: when an LLM-side bash block has decision logic that's mechanical, extract into a script (sync-workspace-step4c.js was the prototype). For workspace-sync, candidate extractions: (a) the smart_copy loop body (decisions are now ~95% deterministic given the prune-deletion set and GIT_APPEND_ONLY array); (b) the run-report writer (already partially a node block); (c) the divergence sentinel logic. Map each candidate by: lines saved from LLM context, behavioral risk, smoke-test footprint.

Q5 — Output volume composition. 24% output fraction is high. What is workspace-sync writing? Best guess: skip-log appends (one row per skip × 65K) + run-report JSON + commit messages. Confirm or refute by looking at the actual transcript outputs across 3-5 runs. If skip-log writes dominate, that's a candidate to batch (write a summary row vs per-skip row).

Q6 — Cadence reduction option. Workspace-sync runs hourly during active windows (15-24×/day after PEAK-SHIFT 2026-06-08). Could it run every 2 hours during active hours and still maintain rescue latency budget? Rescue latency is the critical metric — current 1h is well-margined for decider 403 push failures. 2h would still be acceptable. Halving runs = halving cost.

Q7 — PROP-051 disaster-sensitivity. workspace-sync.md is the file that exploded 2026-05-21 (workspace-sync mass-delete disaster). Any change here MUST honor PROP-051 fail-closed gates A1-A4 + PROP-103 trust gate + the clone hygiene PROP-051 Workstream B. Investigation is read-only / propose-only; integration ships with disaster-grade smoke testing.

Q8 — Compare to non-cost benefits. Workspace-sync is the single point of guarantee for FUSE→git rescue of decider 403s. Reducing its cycles or trimming its work might reduce rescue coverage. The Phase 0 measurement should quantify the rescue events the agent has caught per week so we have a baseline against which to evaluate proposed slims.
deliverable: A PROP-NNN proposal in monitor/tinker/proposals/ with: (1) Q1 per-turn token map; (2) Q2 skip-loop attribution; (3) Q3 workspace-sync vs dome-mirror comparison; (4) Q4 helper-script extraction candidates with risk + lines-saved estimates; (5) Q5 output-volume breakdown; (6) Q6 cadence-reduction analysis with rescue-latency budget check; (7) Q7 PROP-051 sensitivity acknowledgment + smoke-test plan; (8) Q8 rescue-event baseline. Phased rollout: Phase 0 = measurement + shadow-mode helper-script if scope allows; Phase 1 = the actual slim, conditional on Phase 0 evidence + PROP-051-grade smoke-test signoff. Propose-only; operator integrates after review.
constraints: PROP-051 disaster-sensitivity: workspace-sync.md is the file that produced the 2026-05-21 mass-delete event. Any prompt edit must honor PROP-051 gates A1-A4. Any Phase 1 integration ships with operator smoke-test + 7-day shadow.

Don't touch the prune-resurrection guards (PROP-094/099/103). The 65K-skip volume IS doing real work — preventing FUSE→git resurrection of pruned files. The lever is making the LLM not have to MANUALLY DECIDE on each one, not removing the guard.
Don't propose 'kill cost-history-from-workspace-sync' as the lever. workspace-sync's cost-history is itself one of the data sources we need to keep instrumented.
Q6 cadence-reduction is the cheapest possible fix but trades against rescue latency. Honor that trade-off explicitly — don't recommend it without the rescue-event baseline from Q8.
Keep PROP-104 Phase 0 instrumentation pattern in mind. The STEP_MARKER stderr breadcrumb pattern proved its worth for decider; same shape works for workspace-sync. Cheap and reversible.

background_artifacts.comparison_baseline_dome_mirror: 62 rows × $0.73/run × 15-runs/day = $11/day at 5 turns/run (workspace-sync: 41 rows × $2.18/run × 15-runs/day equivalent = $13/day at 21 turns/run)
related_prop_lineage: PROP-051 (workspace-sync disaster postmortem + safety gates A1-A4 + clone hygiene + integrity pruning). This directive's deliverable MUST not regress PROP-051.

PROP-066 (sync-workspace-step4c.js helper-script extraction). The proven pattern for moving load-bearing bash blocks out of the LLM and into deterministic scripts. Workspace-sync.md has more candidates of the same shape.
PROP-094 / PROP-099 / PROP-103 (prune-resurrection guard discipline). The 65K-skip volume is THIS work; do not remove it.
PROP-104 (decider working-set reduction Phase 0 measurement pattern). The STEP_MARKER breadcrumb instrumentation is directly transferable.
PROP-021 (curmudgeon dispatcher precompute-and-slim). The precedent for 'measure first, ship Phase 1 conditional on Phase 0 evidence' that this directive should mirror.

not_in_scope: dome-mirror cost analysis (sibling agent, different surface). If Q3 comparison surfaces dome-mirror inefficiency, separate directive.
Switching workspace-sync's model. Same out-of-scope as PROP-021's curmudgeon investigation — operator decides separately.
Removing rescue guarantees. The 1h rescue latency for decider 403 push failures is the load-bearing capability.
